subject: biology
title: Evolution by natural selection
key_idea: Individuals in a population vary. Those with characteristics best suited to the environment are more likely to survive and reproduce, passing on their alleles. Over many generations the population changes. This is evolution by natural selection.

blocks.text: Charles Darwin explained how species change over time. This section covers the key terms.

items.meaning: A change in the inherited characteristics of a population over time, through natural selection. It may result in a new species.
The process by which organisms best suited to their environment survive and reproduce, passing on their alleles.
A factor that makes some individuals more likely to survive, such as predators, disease, competition for food or a change in the environment.

items: All species of living things have evolved from simple life forms that first developed more than three billion years ago.
Natural selection acts on **variants** whose phenotypes are best suited to their environment.
**Speciation:** if two populations of one species become so different in phenotype that they can no longer interbreed to produce fertile offspring, they have formed two new species.
Evolution is easier to study in species with a short life cycle and many offspring, because the population changes faster.
Evolution is a change in the inherited characteristics of a population over time.
Natural selection is the process that drives it.
Selection pressures decide which individuals survive.

blocks.text: Natural selection follows the same steps each time. Put them in order to test yourself.

diagram.alt: Put the steps of natural selection in order.
steps: Individuals in a population show variation, caused by mutations and different alleles
More offspring are produced than can survive, so selection pressures such as competition for food or predators act
Individuals with characteristics best suited to the environment are more likely to survive
They pass on the alleles for the useful characteristic to their offspring
Over many generations the allele becomes more common in the population

items: Pass on **alleles** or genes. Saying "pass on the characteristic" is not enough.
Mutations happen at random. They do not happen because an organism needs them.
The change takes many generations.
Variation, survival of the better adapted, reproduction, passing on alleles.
Mutations are random. Selection is not.
Repeat over many generations and the population changes.

sections.heading: Using the idea in an example

blocks.text: Exam questions give an example and ask you to apply the steps. Use the example's own details at each step.

items: There is variation in beak length, caused by mutations.
Bird feeders are a selection pressure.
Birds with longer beaks reach more nuts, so they get more food and energy.
They are more likely to survive and reproduce.
They pass on the allele for a long beak.
Over many generations the mean beak length increases.
A mutation produces a black mouse.
Black mice are better camouflaged on black rock.
They are less likely to be eaten by snakes or owls.
They survive to reproduce and pass on the gene for black colour.
Name the variation, the selection pressure and the advantage.
Say the better adapted survive and reproduce, and pass on the allele.
Finish with over many generations.

checks.q: Describe the process of natural selection.
checks.a: There is variation between members of a species. Those better adapted survive and reproduce. They pass on their favourable alleles to their offspring.

checks.q: What is a selection pressure? Give one example.
checks.a: A factor that makes some individuals more likely to survive than others. For example, predators, disease or competition for food.

checks.q: Why is it wrong to write that a bird "needed" a longer beak so a mutation happened?
checks.a: Mutations occur at random. Natural selection then favours birds that happen to have the useful allele.

worked_example.question:
Modern fish species have evolved from fish that lived a long time ago. Evolution is caused by mutation and natural selection.

Describe the process of natural selection.
answer_points: There is variation between members of a species.
The better adapted survive (survival of the fittest).
They reproduce and pass on the favourable alleles, genes or mutations.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each stage. "Pass on characteristics" is ignored.

worked_example.question: Describe the theory of evolution by natural selection.
answer_points: Offspring are overproduced.
Organisms in a species show variation (or mutations).
There is a struggle for existence, a selection pressure or competition.
The adapted organisms survive.
Their offspring inherit the characteristic, gene or allele.
This is repeated over many generations.
worked_example.tip: Any three of the six points score one mark each.

worked_example.question:
In most areas of Mexico the ground is covered in grey rocks. In one area the ground is covered with black rocks. The black rocks were formed about 1000 years ago when a volcano erupted.
The scientists make two observations:
1. Very occasionally a black mouse is born to grey parents due to a mutation.
2. Black mice are well camouflaged.

Using these two observations, explain why most of the mice in this area are black and not the usual grey.
answer_points: The process involves natural selection.
The mice are fed on by snakes or owls.
Black mice are less likely to get eaten by snakes or owls.
They can pass on the gene for black colour.

worked_example.question:
Monkey flower plants were introduced to Europe from North America about 200 years ago.
Ancestors of monkey flower plants had a much smaller leaf area.
Explain how the monkey flower plants have developed a larger leaf area over time.
answer_points: Mutation produced a larger leaf area.
Natural selection acts on the variation.
Many offspring are produced, so there is competition for light and other resources.
Plants with a larger leaf area have a survival advantage and are better adapted.
Larger leaves absorb more light for photosynthesis.
Plants with larger leaves reproduce and pass on the alleles for a larger leaf area.
This happens over many generations until larger leaves are common in the population.

blocks.text: Natural selection must be described in full, and adaptation defined.

items: There is genetic variation within the population.
More offspring are produced than can survive.
There is a struggle for survival, including competition for resources.
Individuals that are better adapted to the environment have a greater chance of reproducing.
These individuals pass on their alleles to the next generation.

items.meaning: (Supplement) The process, resulting from natural selection, by which populations become more suited to their environment over many generations.

items: (Supplement) In **natural selection**, the environment decides which individuals survive and reproduce.
(Supplement) In **artificial selection**, humans choose which individuals breed, to get the features they want.
Both depend on variation, and both pass useful alleles on to the next generation.
Natural selection leads to adaptation. Artificial selection is quicker and gives features useful to humans.

worked_example.question:
Sandpipers have long beaks so that they can dig for worms in the mud.
Explain how sandpipers evolved to have long beaks.
answer_points: There is variation in beak length.
Mutation produced the allele for a longer beak.
A longer beak reaches deeper for worms, so the bird gets more food.
Birds with longer beaks survive and reproduce, so they have offspring.
They pass on the allele for a long beak.
